summary: Join our GIS training course focused on Climate Change and Disaster Risk Management. Equip yourself with essential tools for a sustainable future.
lede: Climate risk GIS uses spatial data to assess how climate hazards may affect people, infrastructure, ecosystems, and essential services. For GIS analysts, climate adaptation officers, disaster risk managers, and emergency planners, the course develops practical skills in geodatabase design, hazard and vulnerability mapping, risk scoring, scenario comparison, and dashboard communication to support planning and preparedness decisions.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who already use spatial information or manage climate and disaster decisions, and who need a practical climate risk GIS workflow for assessment, planning, and executive reporting.
modules: Hazard Mapping with ArcGIS and QGIS
prerequisites: You should have working knowledge of basic GIS concepts, including layers, attributes, map composition, and simple spatial queries. Prior experience with QGIS or ArcGIS is useful but not essential. No programming experience is required for completion. Advanced topics such as AI-assisted image classification, IPCC scenario interpretation, and automated geospatial workflows are taught at conceptual and operational application levels, while core data preparation, overlay analysis, risk scoring, and map production receive hands-on practice. Bring a laptop if your delivery arrangement permits it.
